cases.evidence: Degener s.v. šáako gives Arm followed by [Bur. -śák], without an explicit direction arrow. Berger p. 388 has a damaged/merged OCR entry containing -ák and Arm; p. 389 preserves guśák in an arm-breaking curse. These establish a comparative lead, not a sufficiently verified immediate-donor assignment. CDIAL 12376 śākhā branch and 12379 śākhya do not themselves list this Shina arm term.
cases.nextStep: Check the printed Berger arm head and an explicit historical discussion of borrowing direction; do not normalize the damaged OCR or infer ancestry from similarity.

cases.evidence: CDIAL 10512 lists Shina ǰū with the explicit qualification lw. with ǰ-. The selected jū/źū/źuve forms belong to that comparative problem, but the entry does not establish the immediate donor. Retain the source coronal and inflectional distinctions and investigate the donor before proposing an ancestry edge. Rajapurohit Dras jũ is added to this donor search: CDIAL explicitly labels Shina jū a loan with j-. Its compiled gloss says plural while its dialect tag says singular, so number also needs source checking. The further Rajapurohit jũẽ plural louse response is included in the same loan investigation.

cases.evidence: Degener s.v. gáan identifies the lower leg and compares Burushaski -ġáan heel, but does not mark borrowing direction. The body-part semantic relation is plausible; it is insufficient to choose an immediate donor without checking the Burushaski entry and contact history.

CDIAL 1338 explicitly lists Shina ā̃ṭe flour as borrowed from an Indic source (← Ind.). The exact immediate donor is unspecified, so these survey forms are not given reflex links to *ārta. The anomalous āite notation also requires a source check. Rajapurohit āṭe is merged across flour and dough prompts; both meanings are retained, while the immediate donor remains unresolved.

cases.evidence: Schmidt and Kaul (2008), Example 5, resolve borrowing direction for Gilgiti, Kohistani and Drasi; eight records have moved to pending proposal 293. The remaining dialect records still need their own contact and transcription assessment. Degener’s comparison alone does not resolve those routes.
cases.nextStep: Check other dialects individually against the contact discussion; preserve the m/b, aspiration and vowel distinctions. Do not extend the three explicitly identified dialect routes automatically.

cases.evidence: CDIAL 12062’s uncertain Jijal vk comparison with vṛka is revised in numbered addendum 14808 to a probable Burushaski loan. That note separately gives Domaaki urk from Sanglechi wvrk. These are distinct proposed routes: it does not establish the donor of the modern Dras and HKAT uruk/urke forms, which must not be linked directly to vṛka on resemblance alone.
cases.nextStep: Locate explicit evidence for the donor of the modern uruk forms and distinguish it from the Jijal vk and Domaaki urk claims.

cases.evidence: Degener compares Shina būši cat with Burushaski bus, without a direction arrow. The LSI puśī/puśō/buśī series may involve an expressive animal-name family or contact, but the comparison alone does not demonstrate an immediate Burushaski donor or explain the initial voicing alternation.
cases.nextStep: Check the original cat entries and explicit direction-of-borrowing discussion; preserve the p/b and gender-ending differences.
cases.primaryEvidenceText: Degener: H| búuši fem. Katze. [Atlas 30, Bur. bus].

cases.evidence: CDIAL 958 aṣṭhi explicitly places the Shina ā̃ṭi/aṭi bone series under its statement that the remaining Kafir and Dardic forms are borrowed from Indic, citing Morgenstierne. The source does not identify a precise immediate donor, and the remote relation of aṣṭhi to asthi is itself uncertain. These modern nasalized, aspirated and plain variants must therefore remain donor-unresolved rather than be assigned an unqualified ancient reflex.
cases.nextStep: Check Morgenstierne NTS ii 246 and IIFL iii 3, 22, then seek a modern dialect-specific donor analysis.

cases.evidence: Berger’s printed-p. 388 entry compares Shina śōdo and feminine śōdi with the Burushaski monkey word; its OCR head is damaged to adí. Yoshioka supplies the intact Burushaski śadí comparison. Neither compiled comparison establishes the borrowing direction. CDIAL 11515 instead concerns the distinct vandur family and explicitly labels Guresi vandur a Lahnda loan; it does not justify assigning these śad-/śod- forms to vānara.
cases.nextStep: Find an explicit historical discussion of śadī/śodī and its immediate donor; keep vocalism and gender/plural endings distinct. Do not use the damaged Berger head as a donor.
